lesson_title: Puberty Runs on Text Messages: The Hormones Behind the Changes
hook_text: Your voice is not broken. Your voice box is just growing faster than you can control it.
clip_script: Puberty is your body texting itself. It starts in the brain, which tells the pea-sized pituitary gland to send a message through the blood to the testes or the ovaries: wake up. They answer with the sex hormones. Testosterone from the testes says: grow a beard, build muscle, broaden the shoulders, start making sperm, and grow the voice box. The vocal cords get longer and thicker, like swapping a thin guitar string for a thick one, so the voice drops, and while it grows, it cracks. Oestrogen and progesterone from the ovaries say: grow breasts, widen the hips, start the monthly cycle, thicken the lining of the womb. Everyone gets a growth spurt, girls about two years earlier, which is why they tower over the boys in Grade 7. Everyone sweats more, and bacteria turn that sweat into body odour. Everyone's skin makes more oil, and blocked, infected pores become pimples. Not chocolate. Hormones. And it starts anywhere from 8 to 14, so stop comparing.
visual_style: Speech bubbles fly from a brain to a pea-sized gland and down the bloodstream to labelled organs; a guitar string swaps thin for thick as a voice meter drops; two silhouettes grow at different times.
pacing: Quick message chain, a playful beat on the cracking voice, a fast list of shared changes, a firm finish on timing.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and sort the changes into boys, girls and both.
